This page describes the datasets the workshop uses, where to download them, and where to put them so the tutorials can find them.

The workshop runs on **two parallel dataset paths**:

-   **Laptop path (default).** A small two-sample dataset (`ifnb`, \~25 MB, \~14k cells) that lets you complete the entire scRNA-seq workflow — including **integration** — on a typical laptop. This is what the numbered tutorials (01–09) use.
-   **Talapas scaling path (optional).** A larger 20k-cell, 7-donor dataset (10x NSCLC DTC, \~250 MB compressed, \~700 MB extracted) that shows how the same workflow scales up. The companion tutorials live in `Exercise_Folder/Talapas/` and are designed to be run as R + SLURM scripts on the [Talapas cluster](Resources_Folder/VSCode_Talapas.html). Use this path **after** you've worked through the laptop tutorials.

Where applicable, we follow Khushbu Patel's [YouTube Tutorials](https://github.com/kpatel427/YouTubeTutorials) so her video walkthroughs serve as supplementary material.

## Expected directory layout

By convention every tutorial reads from `../data/` — i.e. a `data/` folder at the repository root. After you finish downloading, your tree should look like:

```
scrnaseq_workshop/
├── Exercise_Folder/
│   ├── Tutorial_01_QC_Preprocessing.qmd          (laptop, ifnb)
│   ├── Tutorial_02_DimReduction_Clustering.qmd
│   ├── Tutorial_03_Markers_Annotation.qmd
│   ├── Tutorial_04_Integration.qmd
│   ├── Tutorial_05_DESeq2_DE.qmd
│   ├── Tutorial_05_DESeq2_DE.qmd
│   ├── Tutorial_06_FunctionalAnalysis.qmd        (clusterProfiler)
│   ├── Tutorial_07_DifferentialAbundance.qmd     (miloR)
│   ├── Tutorial_08_Reference_Annotation.qmd
│   ├── Tutorial_09_scATACseq_Signac.qmd
│   ├── Tutorial_10_WGCNA.qmd
│   ├── Tutorial_11_Spatial_Transcriptomics.qmd   (Visium, stxBrain)
│   └── Talapas/                        (Talapas scaling exercises)
│       ├── Tutorial_Talapas_03_QC_Preprocessing.qmd
│       ├── Tutorial_Talapas_04_DimReduction_Clustering.qmd
│       └── Tutorial_Talapas_05_Markers_Annotation.qmd
└── data/
    ├── (ifnb and stxBrain are loaded via SeuratData — no download to data/)
    ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix/                # NSCLC (Talapas exercise)
    │   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz
    │   ├── features.tsv.gz
    │   └── matrix.mtx.gz
    ├── atac_v1_pbmc_10k_filtered_peak_bc_matrix.h5  # scATAC (Tut 09)
    ├── atac_v1_pbmc_10k_fragments.tsv.gz (+ .tbi)   # scATAC (Tut 09)
    ├── atac_v1_pbmc_10k_singlecell.csv              # scATAC (Tut 09)
    └── GSE152418_p20047_Study1_RawCounts.txt        # WGCNA (Tut 10)
```

Tutorials 01–04 do **not** need anything in `data/` to start — `ifnb` is downloaded once into your R user library by `SeuratData`. They only write to `data/` (the chained `.rds` files between tutorials).

## Tutorials 01–08 — `ifnb` (Kang *et al.* 2017, two-sample PBMCs)

**What it is.** Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from eight lupus donors. Each donor's cells were split in half and one half was treated with **interferon-β** for 6 hours; the other half was held as a control. Both samples were pooled and run on the **10x Chromium 3' v1** assay.

-   **Sample 1 — `CTRL`:** \~6,500 unstimulated PBMCs
-   **Sample 2 — `STIM`:** \~7,500 IFN-β–stimulated PBMCs

Total: \~13,999 cells across two samples — small enough to run end-to-end on a laptop, structured enough to teach **integration** (which only makes sense across two or more samples).

-   Reference: Kang *et al.* (2017) *Nat Biotechnol* 36: 89–94, [doi:10.1038/nbt.4042](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042)
-   GEO accession: [GSE96583](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE96583)
-   Distribution: `SeuratData` R package (no manual download)
-   Used by: Tutorials 01 → 09

### Why `ifnb` for teaching

-   **Tiny.** \~25 MB compressed cache, vs \~250 MB for NSCLC. Fits on a laptop with room to spare.
-   **No 10x click-through.** It's distributed via `SeuratData::InstallData("ifnb")`, not from `cf.10xgenomics.com`, so you skip the TOS dance entirely.
-   **Two real biological samples.** CTRL vs STIM is exactly the structure integration is built to handle — a strong batch-style axis (the IFN response) overlaid on a shared cell-type structure (PBMC subtypes present in both samples).
-   **Cell-type ground truth included.** The `seurat_annotations` metadata column carries author-curated PBMC subtype labels, so you can sanity-check your manual marker-based annotation in Tutorial 03 against a real published call.
-   **Real condition contrast for pseudobulk DE.** Tutorial 05 (pseudobulk DESeq2) uses `STIM` vs `CTRL` as a real biological contrast — no synthetic group splits needed.

### Install (one-time)

From R:

```r
install.packages(c("Seurat", "tidyverse"))
install.packages("SeuratData",
                 repos = c("https://satijalab.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))
SeuratData::InstallData("ifnb")
```

That's it — there's no separate `wget` / `curl` step. The data lands in your R user library (\~/Library/R/... on macOS, \~/.local/lib/R/... on Linux) and `LoadData("ifnb")` returns the Seurat object instantly on every subsequent run.

### Disk-space budget — laptop path

| Item | Size |
|---|---|
| `ifnb` raw counts (compressed cache) | \~25 MB |
| `airway` (Tutorial 05 primer) | \~3 MB (Bioconductor pkg) |
| Per-tutorial `.rds` snapshots (`ifnb_preprocessed.rds`, `ifnb_clustered.rds`, …) | \~300–500 MB each |

Plan for **\~2 GB total** including chained `.rds` snapshots, or much less if you delete intermediate snapshots after each tutorial.

## Tutorial 05 (Primer) — `airway` (Bioconductor)

**What it is.** Bulk RNA-seq of four primary human airway smooth muscle cell lines, treated **untreated** vs. **dexamethasone**, two technical replicates each → eight samples (Himes *et al.* 2014, *PLoS ONE*). Standard reference dataset for teaching DESeq2; the same data Patel uses in [`runDESeq2.R`](https://github.com/kpatel427/YouTubeTutorials/blob/main/runDESeq2.R).

-   Bioconductor landing page: <https://bioconductor.org/packages/airway/>
-   No manual download — the package ships with the data:

```r
BiocManager::install("airway")
library(airway); data(airway)
```

## Tutorial 09 — PBMC 10k scATAC-seq v1 (10x, hg19)

Used for the scATAC-seq tutorial. **Same dataset as Patel's** [`scATACSeq_standard_workflow.R`](https://github.com/kpatel427/YouTubeTutorials/blob/main/scATACSeq_standard_workflow.R) and the [Signac PBMC vignette](https://stuartlab.org/signac/articles/pbmc_vignette).

-   Landing page: [10x Genomics — PBMC 10k scATAC-seq v1 (hg19)](https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/10-k-peripheral-blood-mononuclear-cells-pbm-cs-from-a-healthy-donor-1-standard-1-1-0) (do the [click-through](#getting-through-10x-genomics-click-through-tos) here first if you haven't already)

With `wget`:

```bash
cd data

wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/1.0.1/atac_v1_pbmc_10k/atac_v1_pbmc_10k_filtered_peak_bc_matrix.h5
wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/1.0.1/atac_v1_pbmc_10k/atac_v1_pbmc_10k_singlecell.csv
wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/1.0.1/atac_v1_pbmc_10k/atac_v1_pbmc_10k_fragments.tsv.gz
wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/1.0.1/atac_v1_pbmc_10k/atac_v1_pbmc_10k_fragments.tsv.gz.tbi
```

::: callout-warning
The earlier "Next GEM v1.1" re-release of this sample is mapped to **hg38** (filenames prefixed `atac_v1_pbmc_10k_nextgem_*`). The tutorial assumes the **v1 / hg19** release because it pairs with `EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75`.
:::

## Tutorial 10 — GSE152418 (COVID-19 PBMC bulk RNA-seq)

**What it is.** PBMC bulk RNA-seq from a published cross-sectional study of COVID-19 patients (Arunachalam *et al.* 2020, *Science*). Severity gradient from healthy to ICU. Same dataset as Patel's [`WGCNA.R`](https://github.com/kpatel427/YouTubeTutorials/blob/main/WGCNA.R).

-   GEO landing page: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE152418>

With `wget`:

```bash
cd data
wget https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE152nnn/GSE152418/suppl/GSE152418_p20047_Study1_RawCounts.txt.gz
gunzip GSE152418_p20047_Study1_RawCounts.txt.gz
```

From R via `GEOquery`:

```r
library(GEOquery)
getGEOSuppFiles("GSE152418", baseDir = "data")
```

## Talapas Advanced — raw FASTQ processing (Cell Ranger / cellranger-atac)

The [Talapas Advanced raw-data tutorials](Exercise_Folder/Talapas/Tutorial_Talapas_02_RawData_Cellranger.html) start from raw 10x FASTQs and run **`cellranger count`** (RNA) or **`cellranger-atac count`** (ATAC) as SLURM batch jobs to produce the same `filtered_feature_bc_matrix/` directories the laptop tutorials consume.

For practice runs, 10x ships small public test datasets:

-   **PBMC 1k v3 RNA** — \~5 GB FASTQ, runs in \~30 min on 16 cores: <https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/10x.files/samples/cell-exp/3.0.0/pbmc_1k_v3/pbmc_1k_v3_fastqs.tar>
-   **PBMC 1k v1 ATAC** — \~3 GB FASTQ, runs in \~1 h on 16 cores: <https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/10x.files/samples/cell-atac/1.2.0/atac_pbmc_1k_v1/atac_pbmc_1k_v1_fastqs.tar>

Reference genomes (the heavyweight component, \~12 GB each):

-   **Human GRCh38 RNA reference (current):** `refdata-gex-GRCh38-2024-A` — <https://cf.10xgenomics.com/supp/cell-exp/refdata-gex-GRCh38-2024-A.tar.gz>
-   **Human GRCh38 ATAC reference (current):** `refdata-cellranger-arc-GRCh38-2024-A` — <https://cf.10xgenomics.com/supp/cell-atac/refdata-cellranger-arc-GRCh38-2024-A.tar.gz>

Both should live under `/projects/<PIRG>/refs/` on Talapas, not in `$HOME`.

## Talapas scaling exercise — 20k NSCLC DTC (10x 3' v3.1 Multiplex)

The **Talapas Advanced series** in `Exercise_Folder/Talapas/` re-runs Tutorials 01–03 on a much larger dataset to show how the same workflow scales. **Run this only after you've completed the laptop tutorials.**

**What it is.** Twenty-thousand dissociated tumor cells (DTCs) pooled from **seven non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) donors**, run on the 10x Chromium **3' v3.1** assay with **CellPlex multiplexing** (CMO hashing). Every cell carries a gene-expression profile *and* a sample-of-origin barcode — so downstream you get both heterogeneity and donor-level structure to integrate.

This is the **same dataset Patel uses** in [`singleCell_standard_workflow.R`](https://github.com/kpatel427/YouTubeTutorials/blob/main/singleCell_standard_workflow.R).

-   Landing page: [10x Genomics — 20k NSCLC DTC, 3' v3.1 Multiplex](https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/20-k-mixture-of-nsclc-dt-cs-from-7-donors-3-v-3-1-multiplex-3-1-standard-6-0-0)
-   Reference genome: GRCh38 (human)
-   Cell count: \~20,000 post-filter cells across 7 donors
-   Used in: Talapas Advanced series (`Exercise_Folder/Talapas/`)

### Getting through 10x Genomics' click-through TOS

The 10x CDN at `cf.10xgenomics.com` serves dataset files **but returns HTTP 403** to a fresh `wget`/`curl` until you've accepted 10x's terms-of-use click-through at least once from a browser on the same network.

The first time you hit any 10x dataset, do this:

1.  Open the dataset's landing page in a normal web browser (links above).
2.  Scroll to the **Output and supplemental files** section. Click **Download** on any file you want.
3.  10x will pop up a *Sign in or share data with us* dialog — accept it. The download starts.
4.  You can cancel that download — the click-through has unlocked the CDN for your session. Now `wget`/`curl` against the same URL works from your terminal, including over SSH from a cluster login node.

If you're operating from a fresh cluster account where no browser is available, the easiest workaround is to download once on your laptop, then `scp` or `rsync` the file to the cluster.

::: callout-tip
**Verification.** A working URL responds with `200 OK` and a content-length matching the file size. A blocked URL responds with `403` and a tiny body (\~21 bytes). Use `curl -sI <url>` to check.
:::

### Download — filtered matrix (\~250 MB)

```bash
mkdir -p data && cd data

wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/6.0.0/20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex/20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex_count_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz

tar -xzf 20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex_count_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz
ls filtered_feature_bc_matrix/
# barcodes.tsv.gz  features.tsv.gz  matrix.mtx.gz
```

::: callout-tip
**Optional — raw matrix (\~1.5 GB).** If you want to practice running EmptyDrops yourself, also pull the raw HDF5:

```bash
wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/6.0.0/20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex/20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex_count_raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5
```
:::

## Tutorial 11 — `stxBrain` (10x Visium adult mouse brain)

**What it is.** Two 10x Visium sections from the same adult mouse brain — one **anterior** (\~2,700 spots) and one **posterior** (\~3,300 spots). Each spot is \~55 µm and captures the transcripts from \~1–10 cells underneath. Total ≈ 6,000 spots across two sections, \~50 MB on disk.

-   Distribution: `SeuratData::InstallData("stxBrain")` (no manual download, no 10x click-through)
-   Used in: Tutorial 11 (Spatial Transcriptomics)
-   Reference: 10x Genomics public Visium dataset; workflow follows the [Seurat spatial vignette](https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/spatial_vignette).

```r
SeuratData::InstallData("stxBrain")
ant  <- LoadData("stxBrain", type = "anterior1")
post <- LoadData("stxBrain", type = "posterior1")
```

The anterior + posterior pair mirrors the two-sample structure of `ifnb`: same biology, two batches, perfect for teaching the Visium-flavoured integration workflow.

## Reference / annotation datasets (no manual download)

These are loaded automatically by the relevant R packages on first use — you don't need to download them manually, but they do need an internet connection the first time.

| Reference | Loaded by | Used in |
|---|---|---|
| `HumanPrimaryCellAtlasData()` | `celldex` | Tutorial 08 (SingleR — Seurat default reference path) |
| Azimuth `pbmcref` | `Azimuth` / `SeuratData` | Tutorial 06 |
| `EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75` | Bioconductor | Tutorial 07 (scATAC) |

## Disk-space budget — full workshop

| Path | Compressed | Extracted |
|---|---|---|
| **Laptop path (`ifnb` + airway)** | \~30 MB | \~30 MB |
| Per-tutorial `.rds` snapshots (laptop path) | — | up to \~2 GB if you keep them all |
| **Talapas scaling exercise (NSCLC filtered)** | \~250 MB | \~700 MB |
| **Talapas scaling exercise (NSCLC raw `.h5`, optional)** | \~1.5 GB | \~1.5 GB (single file) |
| Tutorial 09 — PBMC 10k scATAC-seq | \~2.5 GB | \~5 GB |
| Tutorial 10 — GSE152418 raw counts | \~7 MB | \~80 MB |
| Reference data (cached) | — | \~500 MB |

For a **laptop-only workshop** doing Tutorials 01–07, plan for **\~3 GB total** including reference caches and intermediate `.rds` files. Add the Talapas Advanced series on top and you're at **\~5 GB**; the full ATAC + WGCNA suite pushes the total to \~12 GB.

## "I still can't download from 10x"

If `curl` / `wget` returns HTTP 403 even after the click-through, the most common causes are:

-   You're on a different network than the one where you accepted the click-through (the gating is per IP / network).
-   You're trying to pull a file from the *wrong* dataset variant — there are two NSCLC datasets with similar names; make sure your URL slug contains `multiplex-3-1-standard-6-0-0` and not `with-intronic-reads`.
-   Your URL has a typo. Double-check by `curl -sI <url>`: a real file responds with `200` and a `content-length` matching GB-sized data; a typo'd URL responds with `403` and a 21-byte body.

If you're behind a restrictive network, all of the files above are also mirrored on the workshop's Talapas project directory `/projects/<PIRG>/scrnaseq_workshop/data/` once your account is set up — copy from there with `scp` or work directly on the cluster.
